cells.tense: The strength to hold and finish is here, leading with steady hands.
cells.act: keep the connection coherent while it is hard
cells.ask: While somebody is telling you something hard, stay with them longer than feels natural. Don't fix it. Just stay beside them through it.
cells.core:
When you're building something, you know how to hold it long enough to finish. People feel that. You can sit with their feeling while it's still messy, and you don't have to hand them a better one. Strength shows as staying, not as lifting them out of it.

Try that with one person. Let the connection hold while the thing is still hard. You may want to fix it before it's finished. That's the edge. What this asks is a little more waiting than fast running. Staying is part of the building, not a break from it. You build by being there, not by resolving. The thing that lasts is often the thing you didn't rush.
cells.sheetLine: Your strength is staying until it can stand.
cells.verb: Holding what you build until it can stand on its own
cells.place: at the first stirring, before anything has taken shape

cells.tense: In this pause before anything is chosen, strength is pushing toward a shape it can't have yet.
cells.act: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished
cells.ask: When somebody near you is hurt, let the hurt finish before you decide who was right. Wait it out first.
cells.core:
You want to build, and there is nothing to build yet. So strength reaches forward and starts shaping before the material is here. You settle who was wrong before the feeling has run its course. You hand down the verdict and the person is still mid-sentence with it. The push is real, and it is early.

Try letting one hurt finish all the way before you weigh it. No ruling, no repair, no sorting out who was right. You don't have to know the shape yet. The unfinished thing stays unfinished while you wait beside it. You'll know more by waiting than by ruling. What you decide after the hurt has run will hold better than what you decide inside it.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling it fair before the hurt is through.
cells.verb: Holding what you build until it can stand on its own
cells.place: at the first stirring, before anything has taken shape

cells.tense: The strength to hold a thing through was here, and it left the door it once stood at.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Take something you've already completed and set it down as complete. Then give your next hour to the part that isn't done.
cells.core:
You used to hold things all the way through. Now it happens in the past. You remember finishing, and you talk about what you built, and your hands stay off the present piece. The strength hasn't left you. It is standing in a doorway behind you, facing back. The room ahead looks too open to enter.

Start with one ending. Take something already complete and put it down fully. Then let your hands find the piece that isn't done. You don't have to feel strong first. Putting the done thing down frees the hand that was still carrying it. The moment you finish one real thing, the strength comes back in its own time.
cells.sheetLine: You finished once. The door is behind you.
cells.verb: Holding what you build until it can stand on its own
cells.place: at the first stirring, before anything has taken shape

cells.tense: The building is happening through your hands while your name has gone quiet on it.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin something fresh that no one asked for. Keep the first day of it to yourself.
cells.core:
You keep things steady. People stand on what you've built and don't think about who set it. And very little of it feels like yours to claim. The work is real and the making has drifted away from you. The structure stays up because of you, and the credit has wandered off somewhere else.

Pick something new — small, not for anybody — and begin it before you tell a soul. Not because it's secret, but because the beginning is where your own name comes back. You don't need anyone watching yet. Starting something no one asked for puts the pen back in your own hand. The spark is yours first.
cells.sheetLine: You build it. Someone else gets named.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim: I read the balanced face as strength that waits with what is unfinished, and seed-and-structure implies 'endures' means lasting rather than just constructing. A reader could say no — for me building is only starting things, and Let one person's feeling be finished means nothing. The ask stays useful even if the read is wrong: it is a small noticing anyone can try, and its only claim is that staying with what is done changes what the person hands over. The sentence that serves me more than the person: 'not a lookout scanning for the next thing' — it reads as a diagnosis of their attention rather than an offer they can refuse.
